p: Sure. I would consult with counsel and the general counsel of DOI regarding any such instances, and I would follow whatever recusal advice I was given.
So it's no-- not necessarily-- you won't necessarily recuse yourself from those investigations. Is that right?

Sitting here today, I can't anticipate every possible scenario that might come

up, but what I can commit to is consulting with counsel and following any recusal advice I'm given... (CROSS-TALK)
If at any moment the DOI, my apologies if-- if at any moment the Chief Counsel were ever to be investigated, would you recuse yourself from that?
As I said, I would consult with counsel. I think in those circumstances that's likely. But what I would do is consult with general counsel and follow that advice.

The Mayor's transition team consisted of 400 people who were brought together to recruit talent to the administration. Did you have any direct involvement with the members of the transition team during the selection process, or do you only deal with staff?
During the selection process, did I-- Sorry, can you repeat the question?
Yeah, of course. Did you have any direct involvement with the members of the transition team during the selection process, or did you only deal with staff?

I dealt with staff. I think at one point, after I had submitted my application for the position, I received a call from someone on the transition team just to acknowledge receipt of the application materials, and they asked me one or two questions... (CROSS-TALK)
But your first contact was with staff, is that correct?
Correct.
Did your relationship with the Council to the Mayor allow you to bypass the members of the transition team during the selection process? My understanding is, yes.
I don't know what the procedures are with the transition team, so I'm not in a position to answer that.

Okay. You said in your pre-hearing questions that the Mayor's counsel asked you to apply for the job, that it wasn't your idea. If you were looking to hire people for their independence, would you hire someone with whom you've been friends for almost half your life? Or will you try to conduct outreach beyond your immediate circle?
So I think that mischaracterizes what transpired.
Okay.

The Chief Counsel contacted me to see if I might be interested in the position based on-- I believe he contacted me based on my skill and experience for the job. He didn't encourage me to apply. He didn't ask me to apply. He asked me if I was interested. I considered whether I was, and then I submitted an application.
Were you interested before he-- before that request came in?
Before he contacted me, I did see in the news that the previous DOI Commissioner had left her position, and I had thought about it briefly.
And why didn’t you apply before that?
That was a few days before he reached out to me.

Has Mr. Kassem or anyone else working for the Mayor suggested that there are individuals that they would recommend for

employment at DOI? If not, do you think it would be appropriate for them to make such recommendations?
They have not. And I intend to make independent decisions about who is employed at
Why did you decide to leave the US Attorney's Office?

I had been at the US Attorney's office for about 11 and a half years. I had conducted and supervised countless investigations, prosecutions, and appeals. I felt like I had reached my potential at that job, and it was also time to let other people have leadership opportunities there. Another colleague of mine had decided to leave before me. We had started to talk about potentially opening up a small law firm. That prospect was interesting to me at the time, and I decided I wanted to pursue that.

You reported that you left your law firm in September of 2025. Your former partner reported that in August of 2025, the firm (INAUDIBLE) one or more clients involved in the BHRAGS [Home Care Corp] matter, the BHRAGS matter that is currently before the DOI. Who are these

clients, and in what capacity are these clients involved in the matter? Are they targets?

So I was not aware of that involvement, but my understanding, which I learned just a few days ago after the indictment became public, is that the firm or a partner in the firm was... is pool counsel to employees, uh, employed by one of the nonprofits.
Do you intend to discuss these matters with COIB or DOI during your vetting process?
Sorry, can you repeat the question?
Have you discussed these matters with COIB or DOI during your vetting process?
I have not. I was not aware of the representation until two days ago.
And if confirmed, what would you do in relation to these matters?
Again, I would seek the advice of counsel and follow any recusal advice.
Thank you, Chair.
Thank you. I would like to turn it over to Minority Leader Carr.

Thank you, Chair. Ms. Shihata, thank you for being with us today and answering all of our questions and for your testimony. I want to talk a little bit about your time in public service and then in the private sector. So obviously, you have significant public service experience coming into this appointment process, and you talked a little bit about this in your pre-hearing question responses. Why return to public service now when it seems like, you know, you could really go anywhere that you like based on your resume? And, you know, why in particular, DOI?

So, I've always felt most fulfilled in my career when engaged in public service. I think public service is where you can really have the most impact. And I think the work that DOI does is so important to the city in rooting out corruption, waste, and mismanagement, and also helping to prevent those things, that it's really a unique opportunity to make a difference in a city that I love. And so that's why.
Okay. Thank you. You mentioned in your response to the Deputy Speaker's questions that you only donated to one non-federal candidate, and that's the Mayor, correct?
That’s right.
And your contributions to federal candidates over the years, were they to candidates of a single party or were they to multiple parties?
I believe they were candidates of a single party.
And would you identify which party that was?
The Democratic Party—I will say, I have voted in the past for other parties.

Okay, that's good to know. So, I-- you used this phrase earlier in your testimony and then an answer to questions, you know, “without fear or favor”, right? And that's often used particularly for folks who are in or seeking law enforcement careers. And so you'll be returning to a law enforcement role if you were confirmed. Would you commit to acting without fear or

favor, regardless of political persuasion or identity of the people you were investigating?
Absolutely.
And can you talk a little bit about how important you feel that is in terms of your role, despite, you know, coming to the table with views?

I think it's the most important thing. Investigations have to be driven by the evidence, the law, and nothing else. They must be apolitical, nonpartisan. That's how you ensure you're reaching outcomes that are warranted, and it's also how you build trust in your decision making by the public.

So you indicated earlier, right, you contributed to the Mayor, you volunteered a little bit of time for the Mayor. You know, clearly you have a level of investment in his success as the mayor that perhaps some others do not, uh, and support for him and his views in at least one particular policy area—you talked about affordability in your answers. So how do you compartmentalize that political kinship, if you will, with the role that

may have you investigating that very leader and his administration, depending upon the circumstances?

It's what I have done throughout my career, particularly as a federal prosecutor. I have investigated people I have supported in the past. That has not affected my ability to investigate them and reach conclusions driven by the evidence and the law. And that is how I will continue to conduct myself as DOI Commissioner.
Appreciate that. My understanding is that you have at least one, if not multiple, social media accounts that you're the owner or user of. Is that correct?
Yes.
What platforms?
I believe I have a Facebook account, an X account, Instagram, Threads, and Substack, I believe... (CROSS-TALK)
Okay. So, pretty comprehensive list there. Are they available to view by the public?
Oh, I'm sorry, LinkedIn as well, sorry... (CROSS-TALK)
LinkedIn? Okay.
My LinkedIn is public, yes.
But the others are not?
I don’t believe so.
Have they ever been available to the public, to your knowledge?
I think at one point my X account was.
And when did you make that change to the best of your recollection?
When I had an active law firm.

Okay. And would you be willing to make those accounts accessible to the public so they could be reviewed by the public as you go through this vetting process, and of course, the Council, institutionally?

Well, I would say I would be willing to consider it. My social media accounts have a lot of personal family photos and things like that that I would not necessarily want to share with the broader public.

And what about members of the Council who are assisting the

Committee with this investigation-- investigatory and vetting process for your nomination?
I am happy to consider it.

Okay. And in terms of, you know, the resources that you'd be looking for, for the Department Investigation, you indicated in your testimony that you would be broadly advocating for the agency, you know, whatever the agency needed in terms of staffing. Do you have a sense of what that is?

So I watched the Preliminary Budget Hearing involving the Oversight Commission-- sorry, Committee, and the acting commissioner's testimony there. So from that testimony, I'm aware of some of the specifics of the budgetary issues.
So you'd be digging into that more, I guess, if in the event that you were confirmed at that point?
Yes, absolutely.
And do you have a sense of what you'd be doing as we approach the Executive Budget proposal later in the spring, once you had gotten your feet wet, if you were confirmed?
Yes, I imagine I would be advocating for additional resources for
Okay. That’s all the questions I have. Thank you, Chair.
Thank you. We have also been joined by Council Member Riley. Now, I would like to turn it over to Council Member Lee.
Thank you, and apologies for coming late. I was stuck in a meeting, but thanks for being here today.
Thank you.

And I know that these questions that I'm about to ask are similar to some of the sentiments of the other previous questions. So my first question is, how can you assure members of the Council that the public at large--and the public at large-- that you will investigate the Mayor and his staff without bias, given that you and the counsel to the Mayor have maintained a social relationship for almost half your life. And that, Mr. Kassem, is also the person who recruited you to apply for the job?

Well, first, just to clarify, I have been friends with Mr. Kassem for a long time, but I would just like to make clear that it was not a close friendship. It has not been a close friendship. We have seen each other periodically, once every few years, maybe exchanged a few emails once every few years. So I would not characterize it as a particularly close relationship.
Okay. I overheard you saying that as I was walking in, so I just wanted to double-check. Okay.

Sure. But more fundamentally, I intend, if confirmed, to approach being DOI Commissioner as I have through-- as I approached being a federal prosecutor, which is to investigate matters without fear or favor, following the evidence and the law and nothing else.

I actually underlined that in your testimony, because I like “fear or favor”, that's a good notion. One other thing-- well, because in the previous-- I guess the reason why we're asking this also is that it was actually the former DOI staff

that broke the investigation around the previous administration and the previous mayor. So I just want to make sure, obviously, that, you know, when it comes to your role, especially in this particular role, that you will be able to do it without any sort of bias or, you know, skewed perspective. So I just wanted to make sure about that.

And, just to add, I think the work that the prior Commissioner did, and the DOI did, under the prior commissioner was very important, and I intend to try to follow in her big footsteps should I be confirmed.

Okay. If you were investigating public contracts that were supposed to be subject to an RFP, and you found that a contract had been awarded to the friend of the official in charge of the contract, would you stop your inquiry if you found out that the contractor was qualified to provide the services?
No, I think that would still be a matter that should be investigated.

Okay.

In 2025, it was reported that since 2019, DOI has lost a quarter of its employees. As Commissioner, what will you do to increase and maintain the headcount necessary for the agency to do its job?

So I agree this is an important issue, and that the lessening of the DOI’s workforce is something that the DOI Commissioner really needs to address. And so I would start by being a relentless advocate for DOI's budget and explaining why it's so important that DOI is properly funded. I think it ultimately leads to saving City resources, given DOI’s mandate in rooting out corruption and waste. So I think I would start with advocating with the Office of Management and Budget and the Mayor's Office, but also expanding that as necessary to the City Council and the public at large, so that New Yorkers understand what's at stake when DOI is not properly funded.
Mm-hmm.

I think I would also invest time and resources in ensuring that the headcount that DOI has remains there, including by ensuring

that we don't have too much attrition and that DOI is a place where people want to build their careers and stay.
What's the current headcount, and how has that changed compared to previous fiscal years?
So my understanding is that the current headcount is around a little over 400.
Okay.

And I think that includes some individuals who are actually paid by other city agencies. My understanding is that about five years ago, the DOI had a significantly higher headcount, which was, I think, over 108 more positions.

Okay, over 108 more. I know the current chair of our City Council's Oversight and Investigation, as well as the previous chair, have both advocated for a lot more funding in order to have the staffing necessary to do their jobs effectively. And your predecessor actually testified in a budget hearing that the budgetary needs of the agency did not seem to be a priority for the previous mayor. And so, just wondering if you've

had any conversations with the current mayor about his commitment to funding the agency?
I have not, as there is an acting commissioner who is leading those efforts now, but I can assure the Council that that will be a top priority of mine to have those conversations.
Okay, or even in your conversations with the acting commissioner, do you know if that's something that, generally speaking, the agency is trying to really advocate for?
My understanding is, yes.

Okay. Also, what amount would you say would be an increase that is necessary to be able to do the work effectively in your agency? Whether it's additional, how many more additional staff lines, and how does that translate to the budget, if you could give us a sense?
So I want to temper this by the fact that I'm not in fact in the position yet.
Right.

But my understanding from watching the public testimony is that there are, I believe, 26 vacancies currently, and so I think we'd want the ability to actually fulfill those lines. And

in addition, I believe there are some new needs that have been brought up by the current leadership of DOI, including for the investigation into the World Trade Center toxins...
Mm-hmm
that the Council has mandated the DOI conduct.
Okay. And what experience do you have advocating for your own operating budget and how will it-- how will that experience inform how you will advocate for DOI’s budget?

So as I mentioned in my written responses, I did not have a role in securing funding at the US Attorney's Office other than ensuring that forfeiture funds were sought in cases and that certain investigations were designated as OCDETF (Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Forces)investigations. So I have not had that experience previously. But I have been doing my best to get up to speed on how the City budgeting process works, and I intend to rely on the incredible staff at DOI who work on this process as well to inform my decision making in that regard.
Okay, great, you will have a loud voice when it comes to advocating for that.
I intend to.

Yes. Okay. Are you aware that the Mayor's Preliminary Budget provides DOI with the same budget as it had last year? Even in the face of a budget deficit, do you think that's appropriate given the functions of DOI?
I am aware of that. I think I will always advocate for more funding for DOI, given its important mandate. And I anticipate that if confirmed, I would do that, advocate for more funding.

Okay, great. And I guess just my last question, because obviously you have a lot of experience throughout your different roles as a prosecutor running a, you know, a law firm yourself. And have there ever been moments where there was a difficult situation you were in, or a case you were dealing with where, personally, you felt very strongly one way, but obviously, you needed to advocate on behalf of your client? Let's just say when you are a

prosecutor, you know, the higher-ups want you to prosecute the case a certain way, and was there ever an instance where you felt personally like it was different? And how did you work that situation out, or how did you advocate?

Sure. Yes, I do think there were some instances of that when I was a prosecutor. And the way I handled that was to advocate internally for my position and explain why I thought we should proceed in the manner we should.
Okay, great, thank you. Thank you, Chair.
Thank you. I'd like to turn it over now to Council Member Banks.
Thank you, Chair, and congratulations again on your nomination.
Thank you.
How did you hear about the vacancy at the DOI for Commissioner?
I believe I initially saw it on the news.
Have you had any conversations with the Mayor and his team about the expectations of this role?
In the interview process, they asked me questions about my vision for the agency and my qualifications. But it was all in the interview process... (CROSS-TALK)
Anything further discussed that you would...
With respect to?
With the...
With expectations of what I would do...
Expectations, yes.
certain things, for example? No, absolutely not.
You were reportedly contacted by the Mayor directly for this position? Am I...
No, by his Chief Counsel.
By his Chief Counsel? And, for the record, you have contributed to the Mayor’s campaign.
